items.title: 🚨 Anthropic vient de dévoiler claude fable 5.2.
items.summary:
🚨 Anthropic vient de dévoiler claude fable 5.2.

Et il est tout simplement SURPUISSANT !

voici ce qu’il est désormais capable de faire.

1. construire des logiciels entièrement à partir de zéro

un ingénieur d’anthropic lui a demandé de concevoir un système d’exploitation à partir d’un dossier vide.

fable 5.2 a coordonné plus de 1 000 sous-agents pendant huit jours.

résultat : un système d’exploitation fonctionnel, capable de démarrer sur un ordinateur portable, avec :

son propre noyau
des pilotes pour le clavier, le disque et le réseau
un système de stockage permanent
une interface graphique avec fenêtres
un écran de connexion
un programme d’installation

il ne s’est pas contenté de générer du code.

il a organisé le travail, réparti les tâches, testé les composants et coordonné leur intégration.

2. automatiser des migrations informatiques complexes

une équipe d’agents utilisant une version précédente de fable 5.2 a migré un service critique de production de Python vers Rust.

le nouveau service est devenu plus efficace et plus fiable.

son démarrage est désormais environ 26 fois plus rapide.

ce type de travail mobilise habituellement des ingénieurs expérimentés, du temps et des ressources importantes.

3. formaliser le dernier théorème de Fermat

c’est probablement l’une des démonstrations les plus impressionnantes.

une équipe de 1 000 agents fable 5.2 a réussi à formaliser intégralement le dernier théorème de Fermat dans Lean en seulement 30 heures.

la formalisation consiste à traduire une démonstration mathématique dans un langage vérifiable par ordinateur.

le système a construit ses propres mécanismes de coordination et progressé avec une intervention humaine minimale.

à titre de comparaison, Opus 5.5 n’avait réalisé qu’environ 26 % du travail après 18 heures dans la même configuration expérimentale.

4. concevoir des objets électroniques

fable 5.2 ne se limite plus au développement logiciel.

anthropic rapporte que le modèle a conçu trois appareils électroniques fonctionnels à partir de zéro.

il est capable de travailler sur des problématiques de conception matérielle, de géométrie et de circuits électroniques.

il obtient notamment un score de 83,5 sur BenchCAD 2.1, contre 65,3 pour Opus 5.5.

5. faire progresser la robotique

le modèle montre également des progrès importants dans le contrôle de robots physiques.

il peut notamment :

résoudre un casse-tête avec un robot
dévisser un bouchon
dessiner une image
manipuler des objets à partir d’informations visuelles

sur le benchmark RoboDojo, qui évalue le contrôle d’un robot simulé à deux bras, il atteint 64,9 %.

soit plus du double du score obtenu par GPT-6 Astra dans les tests comparatifs présentés par Anthropic.

6. conduire des recherches complexes

fable 5.2 peut également prendre en charge des recherches nécessitant plusieurs étapes.

il est capable de :

collecter et analyser de grandes quantités de données
écrire du code pour tester des hypothèses
coordonner plusieurs agents spécialisés
organiser des expériences
interpréter les résultats
produire des conclusions structurées

l’objectif est de réduire considérablement le travail de coordination et d’exécution qui incombe actuellement aux chercheurs et aux analystes.

7. travailler sur des projets pendant plusieurs heures

c’est peut-être sa caractéristique la plus importante.

fable 5.2 dispose d’une fenêtre de contexte d’un million de tokens et peut produire jusqu’à 128 000 tokens en sortie.

il est conçu pour maintenir un travail complexe sur une longue durée, sans devoir repartir de zéro à chaque étape.

il peut ainsi transformer une demande ambitieuse en un projet structuré, déléguer des sous-tâches, vérifier les résultats et poursuivre jusqu’à obtenir un livrable exploitable.

…⤵️

items.title: Sachverhaltsprüfung: GPT 6 Astra, Aufwand: „max", parallel, mit demselben Kontext: Fable 5, Aufwand „sehr hoch".
items.summary:
Sachverhaltsprüfung: GPT 6 Astra, Aufwand: „max", parallel, mit demselben Kontext: Fable 5, Aufwand „sehr hoch".

Danach Querprüfung: Astra kriegt die Analyse von Fable, Fable arbeitet die Analyse von Astra ab.

Danach: händisch Paragraphen, Normen, Urteile und Co. checken.

Dann: Den ersten Entwurf schreibt Astra -> ich lese und übergebe an Fable meine Einwände -> Fable schreibt neu.

Finetuning mit GPT 5.6 „pro" oder „sehr hoch".

Der fertige Schriftsatz wird komplett, inklusive aller Anlagen, mit GPT 6 Astra, Aufwand: „max", geprüft. Häufig auch zwei mal: 1x im ursprünglichen Chat/Workspace, 1x - in einem neuen Chat/Workspace ohne Kontext.

Kleine Anwendungen, wie z. B. für die Handhabung riesiger JSON-Dateien oder HTML-Exporte, schreibt SuperGrok.

Will ich jammern, jammere ich ins Gemini Pro 3.1 „high".

Also: klare Aufgabenteilung 👍

items.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights. We build RoboScript, a modular infrastructure that implements WICL for agentic manipulation. From a single demonstration, RoboScript learns each task through rehearsal in simulation, freezes the learned knowledge as a Task Memory, and deploys the frozen memory on new scenes with data isolation that ensures every deployment input is available on a real robot. On all 50 tasks of RoboTwin 2.0, RoboScript reaches 83.4% mean success across clean and randomized settings with one demonstration per task and no gradient updates, exceeding the strongest trained action policy by over 20 points. The method generalizes across visual distributions, improves through reflection, scales with the foundation model, and transfers to a physical dual-arm robot through cross-embodiment memory adaptation. With a world in the loop, a robot can learn a manipulation task in its context as well as it learns one in its weights. All code is available at https://github.com/ArcheOne-AI/RoboScript

items.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
items.summary: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration. In mathematics and computer science, large language models have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops. However, quantum algorithms can only be evaluated by classical computers on restricted or small instances. Here we demonstrate automated discovery of quantum programs beyond these regimes including order-of-magnitude improvements on scientific applications. To achieve this, we build a quantum program library in the Lean theorem prover in which Gemini 4 agents synthesize novel programs against formal problem specifications and verify their correctness and cost. Agent teams collaborate, sharing results and knowledge through wikis and discussing ideas at organized conferences. Our results improve on prior baselines for parallel search (up to 2.55x), quantum arithmetic (290x), and simulations relevant to fusion, photochemistry and drug-metabolism by 11x, 8x and 2.5x respectively. Combining human and artificial intelligence at scale, under the rigor of mathematical proof, lets researchers design algorithms that today's classical and quantum computers cannot test, shortening the path to practical quantum computation.

items.title: AI-based characterization of lymphoid structures and the tumor microenvironment reveals lower mature tertiary lymphoid structures, lymph-node follicles, and plasma cells after neoadjuvant therapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma
items.summary: Mature, germinal centre-bearing tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) and mature lymph node follicles (secondary lymphoid structures, SLS) sustain the plasma cell response that shapes outcome and immunotherapy benefit in lung cancer. How this loco-regional axis differs between neoadjuvant-treated and therapy-naive tumors is poorly defined. We analyzed H&E whole-slide images of resected tumors and paired proximal and distal lymph nodes from matched neoadjuvant-treated (neoLUSC, n=20) and therapy-naive (naivLUSC, n=20) lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) patients. Aignostics Atlas H&E Tissue Analysis (HETA) models quantified cell densities per tissue compartment and cell-cell co-localization; a dedicated deep-learning model validated against pathologist annotations detected TLS and SLS and graded their maturity. Prognostic value was tested in an independent cohort (n=458; 46 treated). In neoLUSC tumors, stromal plasma cell density was 72% (p=0.004) and stromal lymphocyte density 48% (p=0.015) lower than in naivLUSC; macrophages and granulocytes did not differ significantly. Total and immature TLS did not differ, whereas mature TLS in the tumor (p=0.034) and mature SLS in the tumor-distal lymph node (p=0.003) were lower in neoLUSC patients. Peri-TLS plasma cell density correlated with tumor lymphocyte density in naivLUSC (rho=0.54, p=0.017) but not in neoLUSC tumors (rho=0.07). In the validation cohort, stromal plasma cell density (HR 0.69, p=0.011) and lymphocyte-plasma cell co-localization (HR 0.66, p=0.004) were associated with longer survival, and neoadjuvant status with shorter survival (HR 1.50, p=0.026). Neoadjuvant therapy is thus associated with fewer mature lymphoid structures and weaker coupling of the humoral compartment to the tumor rather than uniformly lower immune readouts. The stromal plasma cell/co-localization axis is a candidate prognostic biomarker.

items.title: Training Agents to Fail Predictably: Fine-Tuning for Forecastable Tail Risk
items.summary: Before deployment, an AI system might be evaluated on thousands or even millions of inputs, but after deployment it may encounter billions, so its worst failures may not appear during evaluation. Jones et al. (2025) proposed forecasting how risky the riskiest deployment inputs will be by scoring how close the system comes to failure on each evaluation input and extrapolating from the highest scores. We show that the error of this forecast splits into a noise term, whose distribution is the same for every model up to scale, and terms that depend on the shape of the tail of the model's risk scores. These model-dependent terms can make the forecast under-predict badly, both in theory, whenever the evaluation set lacks a rare kind of input that deployment contains, and in practice: on real user prompts marked as toxic, the forecast under-predicted the probability that a response begins with an offensive word for all eleven language models we tested. Because the shape of this tail is a property of the model, we propose fine-tuning the model itself to make the forecast accurate, using the forecast error as the training loss. In a model organism of jailbreaking and in an RL gridworld with rare traps, our method reduced the held-out squared forecast error by factors of 14 to 60, lowered worst-case risk about as much as direct risk minimization (or more), and preserved the model's primary behavior. For settings in which the model should change as little as possible, we show that training with an alternative safety constraint and an added loss term improved the forecast with far smaller changes to the model. Our method also improved the forecast in RL from sampled returns, in language models of up to 8B parameters, and (with minimal-change training) on the toxic user prompts.

items.title: Programming Prescience: Issues in Human Construction of Forecasting Bots
items.summary: AI models' growing capacity for complex reasoning has made them attractive tools for forecasting, or the systematic prediction of the future based on past and present data. However, should AI forecasting systems be adopted, human builders will shoulder the work of building and evaluating them. In this paper, we explore what this work looks like with a qualitative interview study with 15 builders of forecasting bots, sampled from among successful participants in a recent AI forecasting competition. Our analysis surfaces the challenges around (1) tuning a bot to acquire factual research, (2) implementing coherent reasoning, and (3) understanding how well one's bot actually does. During their work, builders frequently introduced complexity that did not pay off, and tested in ways that were opportunistic and piecemeal. Our detailed account of their challenges helps clarify what problems should be targeted in upcoming innovations in process, tools, and human-AI teaming for forecasting.

items.summary:
We built Control Room, a central system to track model workloads across our research infrastructure and stop them quickly when safety or security concerns arise.

It connects every research inference workload, including agentic sampling for model training and evaluation, data processing, and more. This works together with our misalignment monitoring systems, and halts model output within 35 seconds of a decision to intervene to stop or pause a job.

Control Room is just one part of our holistic approach for safe frontier model training and deployment.

items.title: Claude Codeで動画サイトを週末に作ったKarpathy氏が、それでも自分の手でやったのは3つだけだったそうです。
items.summary:
Claude Codeで動画サイトを週末に作ったKarpathy氏が、それでも自分の手でやったのは3つだけだったそうです。

The Decoderによると、Andrej Karpathy氏はHacker News 20年分・4,300万件のコメントをClaudeに仕分けさせ、繰り返し勧められてきた動画6,454本を並べた「HackerTube」を作りました。データの分析からサーバーの設定まで、ほぼClaude Codeが担ったと本人は書いています。続けて作った別のサイトは、4万7,000本の動画を「one-shotted with Claude Code in 3 minutes」だったそうです。

本人が手でやったと記事が挙げているのは、Google CloudのAPIキーの取得、サーバーの契約、ドメインの購入です。記事を読み返すと、この3つはどれも名義か支払いが絡む作業でした。コードは任せられても、誰の名前でお金を払うかは人に残る、という線引きに見えます。なお、元のX投稿の日付は記事に書かれておらず、「YouTubeのおすすめよりかなり良い」という評価も本人の言葉として紹介されています。

丸ごと任せる前に、手元に残す作業を書き出す3点
・APIキーの発行と保管（誰の名義で、どこに置くか）
・お金が動く契約（サーバー・ドメイン・従量課金の上限）
・公開の判断（いつ、誰に見せるか）

週末で作れるかどうかより、この3つを自分で握っているかどうかが、任せ方の分かれ目です。
